title: First-order normal forms: moving negations and quantifiers
summary: Move negations to atomic formulas and quantifiers to a prefix while preserving truth and exactly the free variables.
abstract: To deny that every object has a property is to say that some object lacks it. Such equivalences let us reorganize first-order formulas without changing what they say. We first move negations inward until they apply only to atomic statements. Then we move quantifiers to the front, where their order makes the dependence of one choice on another easier to see. Every formula has an equivalent expression of each kind, with exactly the same free variables, provided structures have nonempty domains. Fresh variable names prevent capture, and a two-element example shows why moving quantifiers to a prefix does not allow us to exchange their order.
